title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
summary: Each value is the height of a bar with width one.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–100,000 bars, with integer heights between 0 and 10,000. Bars have zero-based indices.

statement: Each value is the height of a bar with width one. Choose a contiguous range of bars and draw a rectangle from the baseline across it. Its height cannot exceed the shortest bar in the range. Return the largest possible area.

examples.explanation: The first two bars support a rectangle of height 4 and width 2.
The zero-height bars separate the two positive bars.
Bars 1 through 3 give height 3 across width 3.

constraints: 1–100,000 bars, with integer heights between 0 and 10,000. Bars have zero-based indices.
hints: Conceptual: The shortest bar in any chosen range limits the height.
Directional: Keep candidate heights and their earliest start positions in an increasing stack.
Implementation: When the next bar is shorter, finish taller candidates using the current index as the exclusive right edge. Finish any remaining candidates at the end.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space. Each candidate is added and removed at most once.
